newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean commodity prices seen flat in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Chilean commodity prices seen flat in 1997.

text.p: Prices for two of Chile's main commodities, copper and paper pulp, plus steel are unlikley to recover enough this year affect to share prices for local publicly-traded companies in those industries, brokers Tanner said.
Tanner, in reviewing 1997 prospects for the Santiago Stock Exchange, saw no recovery in prices on those products strong enough to boost the blue-chip IPSA index.

"Continuing the tendency observed in 1996, when they fell sharply, we do not foresee a significant recovery in prices on main Chilean commodities this year," said the brokerage in a statement, referring to copper, pulp and steel.

Paper pulp companies are well-represented on the stock exchange, with pulp and oil conglomerate Compania de Petroleos de Chile SA, or Copec,, alone accounting for about five percent of the selective index.
There is only one major copper company quoted on the exchange, Mantos Blancos.
Another pulp company, CMPC, Mantos Blancos and steelmaker Compania de Acero del Pacifico combined account for about 3.4 percent of the IPSA, said Tanner.

"Expectations for paper pulp prices this year are slightly higher than those on average in 1996," said the statement. No major increases in pulp companies' earnings were expected this year because of the stagnating prices "and their share prices should perform below-market," it said.
Although few copper concerns are traded on the bourse, the red metal is Chile's undisputed number one export, followed by paper pulp and fresh fruit.
On steel, Tanner said it saw no significant increase in steel prices this year, "and for that reason CAP's earnings are likely to stay practically even in 1997," compared to 1996.
CAP's earnings could be helped somewhat by a customs surcharge levied by the Central Bank on steel imports from Ukraine, which last year posed serious competition for CAP, said Tanner.
